summary: August Tholuck worked in religious studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1816–1820), where he later held a post (circa 1823–1826) before serving at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1826 to 1877.
August Viktor Bergny was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He completed his education at Uppsala University, earning his Fil.kand. (circa 1886–1889) and fil.lic. (circa 1889–1898).

August Wilhelm von Schlegel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen under Heyne and Bürger, and later under Chézy and Hamilton. He held posts at Jena (1795, 1798) and the first Indology chair at Bonn (1818).

August Winter was an Indology scholar. He studied under Hermann Jacobi at the University of Bonn (circa 1889–1892) and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau under Alfred Hillebrandt (circa 1892–1893).

August Zacharias Collin worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Lund University (fil.kand. 1856; fil.dr. circa 1859) and under Rudolf von Roth (1874–1875). He served as Docent at Lund (1858) and Lektor at Nicolaiskolan, Helsingborg (1864).

Auguste Ali Bourquin worked in Indology and religious studies. He earned a Dr.théol. from the University of Paris (circa 1883–1885) and held posts at the Royal College of Science, Arts and Commerce, and Wilson College, Mumbai (1882).

Auguste Barth was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Strasbourg under Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann (circa 1853–1856), and taught at Collège de Bouxwiller (1857) and Collège Poincaré Saverne (circa 1860–1870).
Auguste Comte was a philosopher. He was educated at Lycée Joffre until 1814 and then studied at École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.

Auguste Desgodins worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the Major Seminary of Verdun and Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice (circa 1850–1855) and became a missionary for the Paris Foreign Missions Society in 1855.

Auguste Wagener worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bonn under Ritschl and Lassen (Ph.D. 1845–1849) and at Liège (circa 1846–1850). He served as agrégé (1850) and extraordinary professor (1858) at Ghent University.

Auguste-Louis-Armand Loiseleur-Deslongchamps was an Indologist. He studied at Lycée Charlemagne and under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy in 1824, later working in the Manuscript Department at the Bibliothèque nationale de France in 1832.

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Basel, Tübingen, and under Theodor Goldstücker, later holding posts at Jay Narayan Inter College, Cathedral Mission College, Calcutta Madrasa, and Aliah University.
Aung San Suu Kyi, active in Tibetology, studied at Delhi, Lady Shri Ram College, St Hugh's College, and SOAS. She held a post at the United Nations from circa 1969 to 1971.

Aurel Mayr worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University, Vienna, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. From 1873 to 1905, he was professor of Sanskrit and IE linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University.
Aureliano Julio Berriz do Seixo was an Indology scholar. He earned a doctorate in Civil and Canonic Law at Complutense University of Madrid, where he also served as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit.

Awadh Kishore Narain worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under A. L. Basham at SOAS, holding professorships at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

Axel Erdmann was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Uppsala University and the University of Bonn under Johann Gildemeister. He held posts at Uppsala as docent (1871), extraordinary professor (1873–1891), and professor of English (1904).

Axel Klein specializes in Japanology. He studied at the University of Bonn, where he later worked (1998–2007), followed by positions at the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011) and the University of Duisburg-Essen (from 2012).

Axel Michaels works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Hamburg, Kiel, and under Laxmi Nath Srestha, he held posts at Kiel, Nepal Research Centre, University of Bern (1992–1996), and as professor of Classical Indology at Heidelberg University (1996).
Ayako Nakamura works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Hamburg (attested 2009), where she has also served as a Research Fellow (attested 2026).
